- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing the dip.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; if below, overcorrects upward — use 20-day MA as a reference.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after day 15–20, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for days 20–30.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; consider adding 1–2% volatility buffer to forecast extremes.
